popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book XV closes the poem with Venus bearing Julius Caesar to the stars — the comet as Rome's last metamorphosis under Augustus.

popCulture.title: Caesar's Comet
popCulture.description: The daylight comet Romans read as Caesar's soul ascending — Ovid's celestial proof and Augustan propaganda's brightest omen.

popCulture.title: Julius Caesar (play)
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's tragedy ends before Ovid's star, but the murdered dictator and the heirs who claim his name keep the apotheosis in the culture's ear.

popCulture.title: Augustus
popCulture.description: The heir who guards the earth while Caesar becomes a star — Ovid's closing couplet of empire and metamorphosis.
